passage: At nine the night before the engagement, Yogesh found the typed list on the dining table: fridge, gold set, cash for the caterer, "as per custom." His father wanted it couriered to Aditi's family by morning. Yogesh, twenty-two, picked it up. His father was already reaching for the phone. "Papa, wait," he said. "I won't take any of this, and our wedding does not hinge on it." His father frowned. "Many families do it, beta. Otherwise people will say..." "Then let them say it about me," Yogesh replied evenly. "Please don't send it. I'll call Aditi's father myself tonight and tell him so." His grandmother, listening from the doorway, said quietly, "Let the boy speak." The list went into the bin, and Yogesh made the call with steady hands.

qa.q: What items were on the typed list?
qa.a: The list had a fridge, a gold set and cash for the caterer.

qa.q: What is Yogesh feeling when he says "Then let them say it about me"?
qa.a: Yogesh feels determined and calm but respectful. He stands firm despite his father's frown, and his hands stay steady.

qa.q: What did Yogesh do that protected Aditi's family?
qa.a: He stopped the list from going out and called Aditi's father himself to say nothing was expected.

qa.q: How might Aditi's father feel when Yogesh calls?
qa.a: Likely relieved and surprised, since Yogesh tells him plainly, before the engagement, that no dowry is wanted.

grounding: A young man tells his family clearly that he will take no dowry and that the marriage is not tied to it, before the engagement.

passage: On Saturday morning in their Ahmedabad flat, Ojas waited until his mother Hansa had poured the tea. "Mummy, before we meet Neha's parents next week, I need to say something. I won't accept dowry in any form. Not cash, not a car, not a grand hall they have to borrow for. The wedding won't depend on it." Hansa's cup stopped halfway. "Beta, what will Bhabhi and the others say? People like to ask what the girl's side is giving." Ojas kept his voice level. "I know you worry about the relatives. But I'd be ashamed to begin a marriage on a price. Can you help me tell them, or at least not push?" Hansa was silent, then sighed. "Your father wanted the same at your age and never said it. Maybe you'll manage it." She reached across and squeezed his hand.

qa.q: When did Ojas speak to his mother?
qa.a: On Saturday morning, before meeting Neha's parents the next week.

qa.q: What is Ojas feeling as he says he would be ashamed to begin a marriage on a price?
qa.a: Ojas feels resolved and a little anxious. He keeps his voice level but is deeply firm about wanting his integrity.

qa.q: What did Ojas do that made the talk easier for his mother?
qa.a: He spoke early, firmly and respectfully, admitted he knew she worried about the relatives, and asked for her help.

qa.q: How does Hansa move from worry to something like acceptance?
qa.a: She first worries about what relatives will say. Then she sighs, says perhaps he will manage it, and squeezes his hand, showing love and some pride. ❤️

grounding: A young man tells his family early and respectfully that he will not take dowry and the wedding will not depend on it.

"Harsha, the Reddys asked what we're expecting," Nanna said, peeling an orange. "I said we'll discuss."
Harsha put down his tea. "There's nothing to discuss. We don't want anything, Nanna."
"Nothing? People will think something's wrong with you."
"Then they'll think it." Harsha turned to his mother. "Amma, you told me how Ammamma's family was made to pay till they sold their land."
His sister Yamini, nineteen, looked up from her books. "Nanna, if my in-laws asked for a car, what would you do?"
Nanna stopped peeling. "I'd say no."
"Then say no for Harsha too," Yamini said.
Harsha added, "Please call them today, before anyone starts hoping. Tell them the wedding doesn't depend on anything but us."
Nanna looked at his half-peeled orange for a long moment. Then he reached for his phone.

qa.q: What did Yamini ask Nanna?
qa.a: Yamini asked, "Nanna, if my in-laws asked for a car, what would you do?"

qa.q: What might Nanna have been feeling when he stopped peeling?
qa.a: He was probably uncomfortable and thoughtful, realising that he would not want his own daughter's family pressured and that the same should apply to Harsha's bride.

qa.q: Why does it help that Harsha asked Nanna to call today?
qa.a: Speaking early, before anyone starts hoping, makes it clear from the start that the wedding does not depend on dowry and protects the bride's family from later pressure.

qa.q: How might the bride's family feel when they hear Nanna's call?
qa.a: They would probably feel relieved and respected, knowing their daughter is welcomed for herself and not for what they can give.

grounding: It shows a young man telling his family early and firmly that he will take no dowry and the wedding will not depend on it.

passage:
I was the groom, and I was twenty-two, and I thought my family would never ask for dowry. Then, two weeks before the wedding, I heard my uncle on the phone: "A car would be nice, of course, and some gold. It's just custom."
I remember my stomach dropping. Ritu's father had spent a fortune on her MBA. I thought of him receiving that call.
I went straight to my parents. "If anyone asks her family for anything, I'm cancelling the wedding myself." Mummy said, "Sahil, you're being dramatic." Papa said nothing.
I called Ritu's father that night and said, "Uncle, please ignore any requests. We want nothing. I promise."
Ritu told me later her father cried after that call. My uncle didn't speak to me for a year. Looking back, I'd do it again, only sooner, before the uncle ever picked up the phone.

qa.q: What did Sahil hear his uncle say on the phone?
qa.a: He heard his uncle say, "A car would be nice, of course, and some gold. It's just custom."

qa.q: What does Sahil's stomach dropping suggest he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt shocked and ashamed, especially as he thought about Ritu's father receiving that call.

qa.q: What would Sahil do differently, and why?
qa.a: He would speak up sooner, before his uncle ever made the call, because speaking early protects the bride's family from any pressure at all.

qa.q: How might Ritu's father have felt after Sahil's call?
qa.a: He probably felt deeply relieved and moved, since Ritu says he cried after the call, knowing his daughter would not be burdened by demands.

grounding: A young groom looks back on firmly refusing dowry and assuring the bride's family the wedding would not depend on it, wishing he had spoken even earlier.

passage:
Pre-wedding family meeting, community hall office, 3 March.
Families of Samir (groom, 22) and his fiancée met to discuss the ceremony. Early on, Samir's father, Kishore, said, "Of course, the other side will arrange the furniture and a bike." The bride's mother looked down.
Samir said, quite quietly, "Papa, no. We are not taking anything, not furniture, not a bike. I said this at home and I'm saying it here, so everyone hears." Kishore looked embarrassed and said it was only custom. Samir replied, "Then let's start a better one."
The bride's mother looked up and thanked him.
After the meeting I spoke with Kishore alone. He admitted he felt his son had shamed him in public. I asked what he thought his son had protected. He was quiet, then said, "His wife's family. And himself." I have noted that both families agreed the wedding will go ahead with no gifts demanded.

qa.q: What did Kishore say the other side would arrange?
qa.a: Kishore said the other side would arrange the furniture and a bike.

qa.q: How did Kishore feel after Samir spoke up at the meeting?
qa.a: Kishore felt embarrassed and ashamed, saying his son had shamed him in public, though he later saw what Samir had protected.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Samir to say it in front of both families?
qa.a: Saying it clearly where everyone could hear meant nobody could quietly ask later, which protected the bride's family and made the no firm.

qa.q: How does the bride's mother seem to be affected?
qa.a: She first looks down, seeming uneasy under the expectation, then looks up and thanks Samir, which suggests she felt relieved and respected.

grounding: In a note, an adult who watched records a young man firmly refusing dowry in front of both families, protecting the bride and his own integrity.

passage:
Sunday night
Did it. At lunch today, before the engagement talks go any further, I told Ammi and Abbu: no dowry. Not the car, not the "gifts", not anything. I said it clearly, with respect. "I'm your son and I'm grateful for everything. But I won't take anything from Mehreen's family. If her family offers, I will say no, and if our relatives ask, tell them it's my decision."
Abbu went red. He said people would think something was wrong with me. Ammi said it's just tradition, everyone does it. I said, "That's exactly why I'm saying it now, early, before anyone promises anything."
I kept thinking of Zubin bhai. His in-laws took a loan for his wedding car, and his wife still hears about it.
By dinner Abbu said, "Your grandfather also refused, you know." I didn't know. I felt proud and shaky at once.
Imran

qa.q: When did Imran tell his parents about dowry?
qa.a: At lunch, before the engagement talks went any further.

qa.q: How did Imran feel by the end of the day?
qa.a: He felt proud and shaky at once, especially after hearing his grandfather also refused.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Imran to speak early and firmly?
qa.a: Saying it before anyone promised anything protected Mehreen's family from pressure and kept his own integrity, while his respectful tone kept his parents listening.

qa.q: How might Mehreen's family feel on hearing Imran's decision?
qa.a: They would probably feel relieved and respected, free from pressure to give gifts or take loans.

grounding: It illustrates a young man who tells his family early and firmly that he will not take dowry, protecting the bride and his own integrity.
